text:
arjun: Quick sync — rethinking the autoscaler control loop for Dedicated GPU pools. Proposal: split two responsibilities: (1) admission (fast, per-request/lease token decisions) and (2) capacity planning (slower, predictive resizing + headroom). Want to validate assumptions before a big refactor.

sasha: TL;DR on why split? :thinking:

arjun: Admission today is doing both: it makes instant accept/reject choices and also pokes the scaling controller. That coupling causes latency spikes when controller is slow and weird admission oscillation during bursts. Splitting gives fast deterministic answers and lets planner smooth long-term provisioning.

max: Sounds promising. Tradeoffs? e.g., correctness during sustained bursts — admission could keep granting leases and planner lags behind -> overcommit.

arjun: Yep. Two mitigations: (a) admission consumes "pool credits" (soft budget) that the planner refills, (b) admission attaches short TTL leases so long-running jobs must re-acquire or be rejected when headroom drops.

jessica: Also need fairness. If credits are global, big tenants can starve small ones. Suggest credits per-tenant with overflow rules: small-tenant can use global spare only after a cooldown.

tony: We should also plug in a predictive signal (30s-5m horizon) from the demand predictor to preemptively top up credits for expected bursts. Predictor must be best-effort; planner stays authoritative.

arjun: Sketch of admission API I have in mind:

```
POST /pools/{pool}/admit
{ "tenant": "team-x", "gpu_slots": 2, "priority": "prod" }
=> { "admitted": true, "lease_id": "lease-abc", "expires_at": 2212347600 }
```

If admitted=false we return reason: queued|quota_exceeded|no_capacity. Admission should be sync <20ms.

max: Implementation note: keep admission state in-memory sharded by pool for perf. Persist only leases' minimal metadata to a compact KV for cross-node reconciliation.

jessica: On preemption: leases should include a soft/firm flag. Soft can be evicted with warning; firm requires planner to prefer scaling or fallback routing to hosted. We must document SLO behavior.

infra-bot: NOTE: last time we added lease persistence it caused leader election stalls under GC pressure. If we go in-memory primary path, consider avoiding heavy GC allocations (use object pooling).

arjun: Good call — will prototype with object pools in the allocator.

tony: Ops question: how does this interact with burst lanes? Can admission bypass credits for burst-lane tickets? I'd prefer explicit burst-token that is rate-limited and accounted separately.

arjun: Yes — model: 3 buckets per pool: reserved (committed), burst (time-limited fast path), and shared credits. Planner manages reserved and replenishes shared. Burst tokens given by higher-level policy and expire quickly.

max: Monitoring/telemetry: we need per-tenant admitted rate, lease churn, credit balance, and planner lag. Add an alert when admission success rate > 95% but planner headroom < 10% (means we are granting while planner can't keep up).

jessica: Also add an audit log for fallback events (tenant moved to hosted or requests rejected). Important for support.

deploy-bot: heads-up: autoscaler v1 canary is on staging. If you plan infra-level changes, coordinate with the canary window tomorrow 09:00-11:00 PT.

arjun: Action items: (1) I'll draft a short RFC for the admission+planner split with API and lease model, (2) max + tony to prototype in-memory admission shim (object pooling + sharding), (3) jessica builds fairness config and audit hooks, (4) infra team to review persistence fallback. Target: prototype in staging in two weeks.

sasha: SGTM. Put the RFC link here when ready and I'll triage follow-ups. :+1:

arjun: Will do — thanks everyone.
